newsitem.title: INDIA: India state firms get 65 pct primary market funds.
newsitem.headline: India state firms get 65 pct primary market funds.

text.p: India's state-run companies attracted 65 percent of primary capital market funds in 1996/97 (April-March), reflecting investor's loss of faith in the private sector, a market monitor said on Thursday.

PRIME Data Base, the country's top primary market monitor, said in a statement the state-owned companies attracted primary market funds worth 75.39 billion rupees ($ 2.1 billion) in 1996/97, against 50.59 billion rupees in 1995/96.
Their share rose to 65 percent of all primary capital market funds, from 43 percent in the previous year, PRIME said.
"The government has monopolised the resource mobilisation from the primary capital market specially after investors lost faith in the private sector in the last two financial years," PRIME said.

Prithvi Haldea, managing director of PRIME Data Base said the private sector mobilisation had nosedived to 29.19 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 66.63 billion rupees in the previous year.

Haldea said the government's major efforts have been in debt mobilisation. Over the last two financial years (1995/96 and 1996/97), the government mobilised 86.27 billion rupees, or 87 percent of the 99.17 billion rupees of total mobilised debt.

PRIME said a 2.6 billion rupee Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) issue, 24.9 billion rupee issue of Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd, and a 12.37 billion rupee issue of Industrial Finance Corporation of India were some of the largest debt issues in 1995/96 and 1996/97.
However in equities, the share of state-run companies was lower at 29 percent of the total mobilisation of 135.53 billion rupees in the last two financial years, PRIME said.
It said the largest public issues in the last two financial years were those of IDBI (19.35 billion rupees), Bank of Baroda (8.5 billion rupees) and Dena Bank (1.8 billion rupees).

PRIME said that many state-run companies had major issues lined up for future. Some of the main issues are of ICICI (1.43 billion rupees), Corporation Bank (3.04 billion), Canara Bank (7 billion rupees) and Punjab and Sind Bank (8 billion rupees). ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
